name: Islands of Refreshment (1811–1816)
description: A square white field bearing four half-lozenges set on their points — navy at the upper and lower hoist, red at the upper and lower fly — leaving a white lozenge at the centre.
history: Jonathan Lambert, a mariner from Salem, Massachusetts, proclaimed himself sovereign of Tristan da Cunha and its neighbours on 4 February 1811 and published his flag of lozenges in the Boston Gazette that July. Lambert drowned in 1812; Britain annexed the islands on 14 August 1816. A flag believed to be his survives in London.
